sources.entry: LibreDB Studio - Browser-based SQL IDE for PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, DuckDB and more, with SSO, audit trail, ER diagrams and optional AI assistance on your own model key (alternative to DataGrip, DBeaver, CloudBeaver). (Source Code) MIT Docker/K8S
LibreDB Studio | Web-based SQL IDE for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis and more, with AI query assistance

summary.one_liner: LibreDB Studio is a browser-based database editor and SQL IDE that deploys alongside your data and connects to dozens of SQL and NoSQL engines, with optional AI assistance using your own model key.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web-based SQL IDE with a Monaco editor, schema-aware autocomplete, multi-tab workspace, saved queries with JSON backup, visual EXPLAIN plans, interactive ER diagrams, and schema diff with migration SQL generation for several SQL engines. It has a virtualized data grid with inline editing, column filtering, pivot tables, exports, and charts. Analyst tools include an AI data profiler, ORM code generators, a test data generator, and auto-generated database documentation. Admin-only DBA tools cover live monitoring, threshold alerts, one-click maintenance operations, and an audit trail. Authentication supports local login, OIDC single sign-on with PKCE and role mapping, and passkeys. The README states the engine list is 42 and that most non-SQL connectors are read-only by design; an optional read-only agent and Plan mode use Gemini, OpenAI, Ollama, or OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
use_cases: browse and query PostgreSQL or MySQL in a browser
explore MongoDB, Redis, or ClickHouse data from one interface
draw ER diagrams of an existing schema
compare schemas and generate migration SQL
run a self-hosted database editor for a team with SSO
ask an AI agent questions about a database using a local model
how_to_run: On first run, the admin password is printed to the log.
If accessed over plain HTTP on a LAN, set AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=false.
notable: Covers 42 engines through one interface, including relational, document, key-value, vector, time-series, and messaging systems
Agent runs are read-only enforced per engine, with audited execution and cited report claims
Read-only by construction for many non-SQL connectors such as Firestore, Kubernetes, S3, and MQTT
OIDC SSO, RBAC, audit log, and ER diagrams ship in the MIT build
Deployable as container, Helm chart, npm package, or PaaS template
caveats: Several engines are read-only or have missing features (e.g., Druid, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch have no UPDATE; DuckDB has no slow-query or session panels)
AI agent mode only works on a subset of engines and needs a tool-capable model; the agent rail is absent in the embedded npm package
Display masking is client-side only and not server-enforced
keywords: query my database in the browser
share database access with my team
